title: Dr. Agarwals Health Care Ltd - 544350 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Dr. Agarwal's Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 26% YoY to INR614 crores, with Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores (28.5% margin) and PAT margin at 8.9%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered revenue from operations of INR614 crores (+26% YoY, +8.8% QoQ) and Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores (+25.2% YoY), with EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 28.5%. PAT margin expanded 127 bps to 8.9% despite greenfield losses of about INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level. The company commissioned 18 new facilities (16 surgical), a record for a single quarter, and reiterated a FY27 plan of 60 additions including 40 surgical centres. Same-store growth for the oldest cohort (pre-FY23) was 16.3%, driven roughly equally by volume and value.

segments.name: Surgical services
segments.commentary: Contributed 66% of group revenue; cataract surgeries about 74% of total surgeries; refractive about 4.4%.

segments.name: South region
segments.commentary: Largest region at 63% of group revenue; INR387 crores, +22.8% YoY; 189 facilities.

segments.name: West region
segments.commentary: 15% of group revenue; INR91 crores, +24% YoY; 52 facilities including five new greenfield launches this quarter.

segments.name: North region
segments.commentary: 9% of group revenue; INR57 crores, +50.5% YoY; 30 facilities including six new this quarter; Delhi NCR now has eight facilities.

segments.name: East region
segments.commentary: Small contributor at INR16 crores, +21% YoY; 14 facilities; new leadership in Kolkata.

segments.name: Vintage cohorts
segments.commentary: Pre-FY23 facilities INR465 crores (75.9% of revenue, +16.3% YoY); FY24 vintage INR48 crores (+19.6%); FY25 vintage INR62 crores (+38.6%); FY26 vintage INR33 crores. Emerging facilities 21% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Plan to add 60 new facilities in FY27 including 40 surgical centres; Q1 delivered 18 (16 surgical), with 12 planned for Q2 and 30 in H2.
Pipeline of 30-plus signed LOIs supports the full-year launch plan.
Management expects to sustain growth through deeper micro-market penetration, new geographies and adoption of advanced technologies.
Management said a same-store sales growth of 12-13% would be phenomenal, while volume growth is expected to continue at current pace.
Three to five more Delhi NCR facilities planned for the rest of FY27.
Merger expected to close around mid-November 2026.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27: 18 greenfield facilities commissioned, including one large tertiary facility in Thane and 15 secondary facilities; two primary facilities launched in J&K and Tamil Nadu.
Network at 285 facilities across 14 states and 5 UTs and 165 cities; 31% in Tier 1, 63% in other markets, 6% international.
Since FY23, 166 greenfield facilities added; additions rose from 10 in FY23 to 18 in Q1 FY27 alone.
Management said it is working to improve launch pace; some pipeline sites are delayed by compliance requirements.
Doctor headcount at 1,057, up about 23% YoY; about 100 doctors added in last four months, mostly for new centres.
demand_pricing: Q1 surgeries close to 91,000, up 15.5% YoY; cataract surgeries up 16.5% YoY; other surgeries up 13.3% on blended basis.
Growth split: volume about 16% and value about 16% for India revenue; premiumisation about 7.5% and price hikes about 0.5% year-to-date (about 8% like-to-like).

Average cataract realisation has risen from about INR28,000-30,000 four years ago to about INR42,000; Femto cataract adds about INR35,000 per procedure against a license fee of about INR10,500-11,000.
Payer mix: cash 63.6%, insurance and TPA 27.7%, government schemes 8.6%.
Pre-FY23 SSSG of 16.3%: volume about 8% (OPD growth 6% plus about 2% conversion) and value about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue growth came from case mix and price versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: COO Rahul Agarwal said premiumisation contributed about 7.5% and price hikes about 0.5% so far this year, so close to 8% like-to-like value growth against about 15-16% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the losses from new facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Greenfield losses are about INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level, covering FY26 and FY27 centres and including pre-operating losses.

qa_highlights.question: What were the deferred consideration payments and lease interest?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Yashwanth Venkat said about INR25 crores of acquisition liabilities were paid in Q1, and lease liability interest was about INR18 crores; interest on deferred acquisition payables fell to INR3.6 crores from INR6.8 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the North growth only from Delhi NCR?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO Adil Agarwal said Delhi is a new entry, growing from one branch last year to seven now, and Punjab and J&K rebounded from the prior-year Operation Sindoor and flood impact; growth is broad-based across North branches.

qa_highlights.question: Will doctor additions drive future revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the doctor additions are for new centres and productivity should improve as centres mature; senior doctor attrition is 2-3% versus 16-17% group-wide attrition including juniors.

qa_highlights.question: Can realisation growth of about 10% continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth should continue, while value growth depends on lens upgrades and Femto adoption; it could not confirm whether 10% or 8% realisation growth would persist, but the direction is upward.

qa_highlights.question: Why is facility addition pace constrained given cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working to raise launch pace and has a pipeline, but some sites require strict compliance clearances before launch.

risks_watch: Launch pace: 18 greenfield facilities in Q1 against a plan of 60 for FY27 (30 needed in H2 after 12 in Q2); some pipeline sites are held back by compliance clearances, and 30-plus signed LOIs are the stated cover.
Same-store growth normalisation: management called 12-13% SSSG phenomenal and could not confirm whether the ~10% realisation growth persists, versus 16.3% SSSG in Q1 for pre-FY23 facilities.

Greenfield drag: about INR20 crores of losses at corporate EBITDA level, including pre-operating losses, while 16 surgical centres were added in one quarter; margin resilience depends on these ramping.
Doctor productivity: about 1,057 doctors (+23% YoY) with 100 added in four months; group attrition at 16-17%, with senior doctor attrition at 2-3%. New-centre productivity is still to be shown.
Merger closure targeted around mid-November 2026; management gave no detail on terms or impact on the reported numbers.

Delhi NCR and North: growth partly reflects Delhi being a new entry and a rebound from Operation Sindoor and floods in the prior year, and management said Delhi is a long way from South-level maturity.
key_quotes: This new fiscal year commenced with record-breaking results.
Q1 has set the base, 18 facilities launched, out of which 16 surgical, a record for any single quarter in the history of this company.
So, it's difficult to answer whether same 10% will be there or 8% will happen.
We are working on improving the launch pace. I think we have set that benchmark by this quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, volumes and the FY27 facility plan, with specific numbers offered on surgeries, realisation and cost lines. Cautious and non-committal on forward realisation growth and on the pace of new launches, where answers were directional and tied to compliance clearances and future pipeline.
